To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a distributed dynamic topology control scheme that is computationally and communicationally efficient and that it increases the lifetime of the network by more than 40% compared the state of the art.
a new distributed dynamic algorithm called Energy Balanced TC (EBTC) can increase network lifetime by 40% or more over other algorithms, and is as efficient as the best known algorithm.
a novel distributed topology control algorithm called EBTC, which considers the actual power consumed for each transmission/reception, is proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of distributed topology control algorithms that balance the energy consumption at the nodes in order to maximize the functional lifetime of a network.
developing a new dynamic topology control algorithm for sensor networks that is energy balanced, distributed, and that achieves a significant improvement over the best previously known algorithm.
improving the lifetime of wireless sensor networks through the use of topology control algorithms that are energy aware.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithm, EBTC, is a simple, distributed and dynamic topology control algorithm which increases the functional lifetime of wireless sensor networks by a factor of 40% over the best known algorithms in literature.
our algorithm is the first to balance the energy consumption at the nodes and is thus the first to increase the functional lifetime of a wireless network.
the EBTC protocol is an efficient algorithm that balances the energy load of each of the nodes in the network and increases its functional lifetime by over 40%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new dynamic topology control algorithm that is distributed, energy aware and energy balanced.
we have presented an algorithm that is computationally simple and yet provides significant energy savings over previously known algorithms.
we present a new algorithm for topology control which is distributed, dynamic, and has low complexity and is shown to increase the lifetime of a WSN by over 40%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple algorithm can be effective in achieving the goal of increased functional lifetime of a wireless network.
the actual energy consumption for each transmission and/or reception is an important parameter to be considered in topology control algorithms.
the energy consumption for each node is balanced, which leads to a longer lifetime for the network.
